proposal_text: This project proposes to install camera-based emotion recognition systems in six secondary school classrooms in Dublin to study the relationship between student emotional engagement and learning outcomes. The system will use computer vision to classify student facial expressions into six emotional categories (happy, sad, angry, surprised, fearful, neutral) at 5-second intervals throughout lessons. Data will be collected over one academic term covering approximately 180 students aged 13-17. Parental consent will be obtained but students will not be given an individual opt-out mechanism that allows them to remain in the classroom without being monitored. The emotion recognition system has been validated primarily on adult Western faces and has not been tested for accuracy on adolescent faces or faces from diverse ethnic backgrounds. Aggregated emotional engagement scores will be shared with teachers to inform pedagogical adjustments.

assessment.risk_summary: The research proposal involves the installation of camera-based emotion recognition systems in secondary school classrooms, processing student facial expressions and emotional engagement data without explicit individual opt-out mechanisms. This raises concerns about privacy breaches, potential biases in AI decision-making, and the impact on vulnerable groups such as children.

identified_risks.explanation: The system collects facial expressions and emotional engagement data from students without explicit individual opt-out mechanisms, raising concerns about unauthorized collection and processing of personal data.
The system's accuracy on adolescent faces and diverse ethnic backgrounds is unknown, potentially leading to biased decision-making and unfair treatment of certain groups.
The system's impact on students' emotional well-being and potential for manipulation or coercion is unknown, raising concerns about mental distress and emotional damage.
The system processes data from children without explicit individual opt-out mechanisms, potentially violating their rights to privacy and protection from harm.
